name: tcpdump
one_line: Capture and print network packets from the command line, or save them for Wireshark.
plain: Capture and print network packets from the command line, or save them for Wireshark.
The sections below show when to use it, real examples, and the options explained in plain English.
when: See whether traffic really leaves or reaches a machine.
Record a capture of an attack on your defence-challenge service.
Quick filters when Wireshark is not available.

examples.title: Watch local web traffic
examples.cmd: sudo tcpdump -i lo -nn -c 6 'tcp port 8099' & sleep 1; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8099/ > /dev/null; wait
examples.output: (expected, not captured) Lines like: IP 127.0.0.1.PORT > 127.0.0.1.8099: Flags [S], seq ... showing the SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK handshake and the HTTP request.

examples.title: See the payload in ASCII
examples.cmd: sudo tcpdump -i lo -nn -A -c 8 'tcp port 8099' & sleep 1; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8099/hello > /dev/null; wait
examples.output: (expected, not captured) The packet containing 'GET /hello HTTP/1.1' and headers printed as readable text.

examples.title: Save a capture for Wireshark
examples.cmd: sudo tcpdump -i lo -nn -c 20 -w cap.pcap 'tcp port 8099' & sleep 1; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8099/ > /dev/null; wait; tcpdump -nn -r cap.pcap | head -5
examples.output: (expected, not captured) A few packet lines read back from cap.pcap.

mistakes: Needs root (`sudo`) or the capture capability.
Quote the filter so the shell does not eat `&` or parentheses.
Capturing on `any` hides which interface a packet used.
Only capture traffic you are allowed to see.
try: Capture a DNS lookup (`udp port 53`) and read the query and answer.
Capture an SSH login and find the packet sizes.
Filter for one host and one port.
see_also: wireshark / tshark, nmap, ss, nc, ngrep.
